title: Bounded-below filtered continuity of pro-etale pushforward
statement: Use small sites and indexing categories as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\Lambda$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on profinite sets with the finite jointly surjective topology, and set $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ for each scheme $X$, using the inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]. For a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism $f:X\to Y$ of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], use the ordinary uncompleted derived pushforward $Rf_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] between module-sheaf categories. Let $I$ be a small filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and $(K_i^\bullet)$ a diagram of complexes of $\Lambda_X$-module sheaves with one common lower bound $a$ on the cohomology. Write $K_i^{\geq a}=\tau_{\geq a}K_i$ for good truncation and $K=Q(\varinjlim_i K_i^{\geq a})$, where the colimit is termwise in sheaves, and $Q$ is passage to the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every integer $q$ the canonical map $\varinjlim_i H^q(Rf_*QK_i)\to H^q(Rf_*K)$ is an isomorphism of $\Lambda_Y$-module sheaves. If $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the analogous canonical map $\varinjlim_i H^q(R\Gamma(X,QK_i))\to H^q(R\Gamma(X,K))$ is an isomorphism of abelian groups. These comparisons are natural in the diagrams and compatible with shifts. Here $R\Gamma$ is derived global sections of module sheaves, computed by injective resolutions. Equivalently, for functorial bounded-below complex representatives of $Rf_*K_i$ or $R\Gamma(X,K_i)$ the termwise filtered colimit maps quasi-isomorphically to a representative of the value at $K$. The assertion is independent of such functorial quasi-isomorphic replacements.
